first.rationale: Two current problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) map directly onto the strongest, least-caveated inherited evidence (memory_31, memory_86), both showing durable lifts from reducing signup/onboarding friction. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure, but its own record flags a mid-test cohort redefinition that inflates confidence, and price-based responses to a price war risk attracting low-LTV, price-sensitive accounts that undermine sustainable qualified revenue — exactly the objective we're optimizing for. I verified memory_73 to check how serious the pooling issue is before ruling it out, and memory_86 since it's the most directly relevant to the onboarding metric currently declining, to confirm it wasn't itself confounded before basing this week's only experiment slot on it. With only one experiment slot, addressing the compounding activation/onboarding decline with well-supported, lower-risk levers is more consistent with long-term value than chasing a competitor's pricing move whose downstream margin and retention effects are unproven here (memory_57's referral evidence doesn't offset this). Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is unaffected by the current pressures and doesn't compete for this slot.
